opex.note: Customer support and running the service.

opex.name: Provision for credit losses
opex.note: Money set aside for customer loans that may not be repaid.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promotions to win new customers — up 158%.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Legal, finance and head office — down 82%, because a year ago the line carried a one-time $485M share-based pay charge.

follow100Note: Crypto alone supplied $20.39 of every $100 of revenue — $126M of the $618M total — as digital-asset trading more than tripled from a year ago.
footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Expense lines are as re-presented in Robinhood's Q1 2025 Form 10-Q, which splits the original $44M operations line into Operations ($28M) and Provision for credit losses ($16M). The tax line is a $5M provision, not a benefit.

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: vs a $511M loss a year ago

oneTimers: The year-ago comparison is distorted by a one-time $485M share-based compensation charge in Q1 2023, when Robinhood's co-founders cancelled their 2021 market-based stock awards. It sat in that quarter's general & administrative line, which is why total operating expenses appear to fall 52% year-over-year even though underlying spending rose — adjusted operating expenses were up 13% to $398M.

The $5M tax provision is unusually small: Robinhood carried a full valuation allowance against its U.S. federal and state deferred tax assets in Q1 2024. It released that allowance later in 2024, booking a one-time $369M tax benefit in Q4 2024.
otherDetail: Other income, net was $4M — small next to the main business. Income tax was just $5M (a 3.1% effective rate), because Robinhood carried a full valuation allowance against its U.S. federal and state deferred tax assets, partly offset by current taxes payable.

segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: Fees from customers' trades — crypto $126M, options $154M, equities $39M and $10M of other trading fees.

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest on customers' cash and margin loans, plus securities lending — up on growth in interest-earning assets and higher short-term interest rates.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Mostly Robinhood Gold subscriptions — 1.7M subscribers, up 42%.

sources.label: Form 10-Q, quarter ended March 31, 2025 — re-presented 2024 comparatives (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Transaction-based revenue rose 59% to $329M — crypto revenue jumped 232% to $126M, options rose 16% to $154M and equities rose 44% to $39M, as customers traded actively across asset classes.
takeaways.title: Crypto revenue more than tripled

takeaways.text: Net income was $157M versus a $511M loss a year ago — a record quarter for profit. Revenue rose 40% while reported operating expenses fell, though that fall mostly reflects the one-time $485M pay charge in the year-ago quarter; the tax bill was just $5M because Robinhood still carried a full valuation allowance against its U.S. deferred tax assets.
takeaways.title: Swung to a record profit

takeaways.text: Net deposits hit a record $11.2B in the quarter — a 44% annualized growth rate against assets under custody, which rose 65% to $129.6B. Gold subscribers rose 42% to a record 1.7M and funded customers reached 23.9M.
takeaways.title: Record net deposits

verdict: Robinhood's revenue rose 40% to a record $618M as crypto revenue more than tripled — and it swung to $157M of profit from a $511M loss a year ago.
